_README: KNOWN SEARCH MISSES — each entry is a LEGAL schedule that the current scorer ranks HIGHER than
the plan `optimizeAsync` actually emits for that case. They are not bugs in the objective: the
equation ranks them correctly, which is exactly how they were found. They are failures of the
Why this file exists: a search miss is invisible to every gate the project has. `exact-match`
locks in whatever the search emits, so a miss becomes the golden. `self-consistency` compares the
objective against itself. Only a second witness — a plan from a different engine, or a hand-built
one — can show that a better plan exists. This file is where those witnesses live so they are not
lost, and so the search work starts with a concrete failing case instead of a hunch.
How to check them:   node tools/search-witnesses.mjs
How they are found:  node tools/search-miss.mjs <old-sweep.json> <new-sweep.json>
⚠ A witness going green does NOT mean the search is correct at that cell — it means this
particular better plan is now reached. Optimality is a different and much stronger claim; that is
what the enumeration/branch-and-bound programme is for.
⚠ A witness is KEPT after it goes green. `reachedOn` below records when, but the live status
always comes from `tools/search-witnesses.mjs` re-solving — a note in a file cannot notice a
regression. Both entries went green on 2026-07-28 with the entrant floor + the legibility
budget retired (PHASE13 §3.1); they stay so the gate keeps proving it.

witnesses.context: Surfaced by the boundary-credit repricing: swept plans from the pre-change engine, then scored both sets with the new scorer. Every other moved cell improved or tied; this one lost. Unaffected by the 07-27 EPS fix — this cell did not move.
notes: The witness is a repair() FIXPOINT, i.e. legal — verified, not assumed.
★ ROOT-CAUSED 2026-07-27 (PHASE13 §3.1). ⛔ The note that used to sit here — 'the basin is not
being entered at all' — is RETRACTED. It is entered: the outer search FINDS this witness from 20
restarts on, and the finishing tail destroys it every single time. That is why 3/8/14/24 restarts
all return the same emitted plan — more search cannot help when the tail discards the result.
Mechanism: the no-Cold-Snap sub-solve finds Zerk=36, then a groom pass moves it 36->20 for a -46.4
loss, admitted because the QTOL legibility band is measured against a STALE HIGH-WATER MARK
(`val = Math.max(val, pick.v)`) instead of the current plan — the exact defect `challengePass` had
already fixed for itself. The Cold-Snap comparison then pastes an IV chain onto the groomed plan
wholesale, inheriting Zerk=20, and -46.4 becomes -127.2. Nothing ever compares finishLine's output
to its entrant. This is archived PHASE9 §5.17's declined residual coming due.
The landscape: a 2-cell isolated needle on (IV2 x Zerk) — only (45,36) and (46,36) beat the emitted
plan, both single-coordinate half-moves are strictly worse, and a full-grid reachability check finds
NO sequence of single-coordinate moves that reaches it. Both winning regions are genuine 1.0s
plateaus, not knife edges.
⚠ NOT FIXED, deliberately. The clean fix (an entrant floor in the tail) is green on every gate
(search-miss: 9 better, 0 regressions) but makes the QTOL legibility budget unspendable at the top
level, silently reversing the user-directed ruling that aesthetics may trade up to a full cast of
expected damage for a pressable line. That is a product decision, not a search fix.

✅ REACHED 2026-07-28. Root cause fixed, not worked around: `finishLine` now WRAPS in an entrant floor (it may not return worse than it was given) and the legibility budget dropped from a whole cast to a tie tolerance. Emitted score 196760.5 == witness. The 'NOT FIXED, deliberately' note above is retracted: the user ruled that legibility is a display property, so there was never a damage budget to protect (PHASE13 §3.1).

witnesses.context: Surfaced by the EPS boundary fix (PHASE13 §2.5): swept all 25 presets on both engines and scored both plan sets with the new scorer. Four cells improved (two by >0.65 %), one tied, and this one lost 50.8. The scorer did not get worse here — the SEARCH landed in a different, slightly worse local optimum once the press loop's boundary test changed which cast a press lands on. Kael'thas is the corpus's only AoE preset and its longest fight (T=420, ~5 min to solve at 3 restarts), so it is also the cell with the most search surface and the least brute-force coverage.
notes: Both schedules are repair() FIXPOINTS — verified, not assumed (repair(s) == s for each).

witnesses.context: Surfaced by retiring the legibility budget (PHASE13 §3.1). Swept all 25 presets before and after and scored both sets with the same scorer: 11 cells better, 8 exact ties, and this one 127.2 worse. ⚠ Its signature is `IV2 38->45, Zerk 20->36` — the IDENTICAL 2-cell needle as the 1:40 witness, on a 440 s fight. That is the tell: the old `QTOL = castVal` was not only buying co-pressed layouts, it was also letting the search TUNNEL through a slightly-worse intermediate into a better basin. Cutting it to a tie tolerance closed that escape route here, while the entrant floor opened the same basin at 1:40 and 2:00.
notes: ✅ REACHED THE SAME DAY IT WAS RECORDED — and it is kept, because what it proved is the point.
It existed for the length of one configuration: the entrant floor plus a FLAT cut of QTOL to a tie
tolerance. That cut removed the budget's second, undocumented job — tunnelling through a worse
intermediate to escape a local optimum — which is what this cell needed and what its `IV2 38->45,
Zerk 20->36` signature (the 1:40 witness's needle, on a 440 s fight) was pointing at.
The fix was to stop treating one number as one decision: `finishLine` now runs under BOTH budgets
and keeps the better, with the entrant flooring both and ties going to the plan with fewer press
rows. Loose supplies reach, tight supplies tidiness, neither can lose ground. Full corpus after:
11 better, 7 tie, 0 regressions, and -8 press rows / -7 lone seconds / +6 clustering.
⚠ The lesson, which is why this entry survives: a single tolerance had been standing in for two
unrelated policies, and no measurement could separate them until they were separated in the code.
